endorsements.quote: Therefore, any model for integrating LLM-supported consent should include mandatory review of consent interactions by a human clinician, as well as follow-up with a paediatrician.
Before implementing any LLM-supported consent system, healthcare providers must first obtain appropriate parental authorisation for children to interact with these digital platforms.
Healthcare providers must retain ultimate responsibility for ensuring valid consent.

unlisted_practices: Design LLM consent systems to document disagreements between children, parents and providers and automatically flag cases requiring potential court involvement, without attempting to resolve disputes.
Do not program LLMs to repeatedly prompt young people to reconsider an informed refusal of treatment.
Program LLM consent systems to monitor for signs of distress, anxiety, uncertainty and indirect cues of coercion or safeguarding concerns, with protocols for prompt referral to clinicians.
Begin LLM-supported consent interactions with a disclaimer that the paediatrician can access the interaction, and clearly communicate how information will be used and who can access it.
Restrict parental access to LLM consent interactions according to the confidentiality preferences of Gillick-competent or over-16 patients, while keeping complete records for the healthcare team.
Refer users who raise questions or reveal information beyond the consent process to their paediatrician.
Require robust authentication and clear information-sharing protocols in paediatric LLM consent systems.
Implement age-appropriate verification and structured decision-making supports in paediatric LLM consent systems.
Rigorously test automated flagging systems across diverse populations and cultural communication patterns to avoid perpetuating health disparities.
Do not use LLMs to independently assess children's decision-making capacity or Gillick competence.

screen.reason: Ethical analysis and commentary exploring the implications and potential safeguards for using large language models to assist with paediatric informed consent.
